name: Hylton
bio: A member of Wilde's Paris circle in December 1898, who arrived at the Hôtel d'Alsace 'with his boy Herbert' and whom Wilde found almost impossible - 'a sort of grown-up man with a hysterical womb', who made scenes with Sir John Ashton 'like a woman with child'.
bio_note: Added 2026-08-06, found by reading printed 1107 whole after the General Index sent me there for Alphonse. **He is indexed nowhere** - neither in the Index of Recipients nor under his own name in the General Index - and would never have been found by any search. GROUPED later rather than liaisons because he is the adult party here, not the young one. WILDE'S DESCRIPTION IS WORTH KEEPING FOR ITS OWN SAKE: 'a sort of grown-up man with a hysterical womb... like a woman with child' is Wilde using the period's medical vocabulary of female hysteria against another man, in a private letter, in the year after his own release. THE FOLIO IS A CENSUS OF THE PARIS EXILE HOUSEHOLD in December 1898 and should be read as one: Sir John Ashton and his 'little friend' Joseph (both already on this map, connected on this same page), Turner's 'little friend' Alphonse, and Hylton with 'his boy' Herbert. Four young men in three sentences, all described to Wilde's closest correspondent in the same possessive formula. See [[herbert]].
